newsitem.title: FRANCE: Balladur favours shrinking French state payroll.
newsitem.headline: Balladur favours shrinking French state payroll.

text.p: Edouard Balladur, ex French prime minister and member of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR party, said in an interview published on Monday that savings of about 10 billion francs could be made by non-renewal of 10,000 civil service jobs left vacant yearly through departures.

Balladur was commenting in Le Monde newspaper in response to a question on whether he recommended going further than the 5,000 non-renewed jobs which is taken as the centre-right government's basic target for slimming public service numbers.
"With 10,000 non-renewed jobs per year, the cumulative savings would be in the region of 10 billion francs. I want us to go as far as possible in this direction, and further," he told Le Monde.

Balladur, who lost to Chirac in a bid for the presidency in 1995, is seen as one of several potential candidates for prime minister if the RPR/UDF coalition wins a parliamentary election being held in two rounds on May 25 and June 1.
